summary: Applies translate, rotate, and scale operations to POP attributes, most commonly P and N. It can transform point, vertex, or primitive float3 attributes, use Weight attributes, map attributes to parameters, align to bounds, or use an external transform matrix.

key_concepts: Transform POP can transform P and N as geometry, or transform selected float3 attributes on point, vertex, or primitive classes.
Transform order, rotate order, pivot, uniform scale, inversion, matrix multiplication, and look-at controls define the composed transform.
Group, weight, alignment, and map controls let transforms affect subsets or vary per element without leaving the POP workflow.
common_gotchas: Normals need the right interpretation; Transform POP can update N as well as P.
Mapped per-point parameters can make every point receive a different transform, so validate bounds after mapping.
Transform order and rotate order can materially change the result.
